identity.description: Decomposable curve-fit forecaster: piecewise-linear (or logistic) trend with automatic changepoints + Fourier-series seasonalities + holiday effects, fit as a regression on time via Stan MAP. Regression-on-timestamps rather than lag-recursion — which is why it tolerates gaps and irregular sampling that break ARIMA/ETS.

axes.note: deterministicFit holds for the default MAP (L-BFGS) path; mcmc_samples>0 switches to stochastic full-Bayes sampling

consumes.note: timestamped (ds, y) observations; a regular gap-free grid is NOT required — Prophet regresses on the timestamp itself

emits.note: yhat with native [yhat_lower, yhat_upper] intervals from simulated trend-changepoint uncertainty; the per-timestamp trend/seasonal/holiday decomposition rides along as paramsAsOutput 'components' (see portTypeProposal for a first-class port)

portTypeProposals.name: series-components
portTypeProposals.carriedBy: per-timestamp additive decomposition (trend, per-seasonality, holiday effect series)
portTypeProposals.rationale: Prophet's decomposition is a per-timestamp SERIES product, not per-model scalars — 'coefficients' misdescribes it and 'forecast-series' hides it; a distinct port would let downstream diagnostics/detrenders consume components directly. Until ruled SAME/ADAPTER-RELATED/DISTINCT by the cross-model study, it is carried only as paramsAsOutput on the forecast-series emit.

growth.note: structural choice, not searched — logistic requires a user-supplied capacity cap column

changepoint_prior_scale.note: THE flexibility knob — trend-changepoint sparsity (Laplace prior scale); the vendor-documented primary tuning parameter

seasonality_mode.note: multiplicative for series whose seasonal swing grows with level

n_changepoints.note: candidate changepoint count; regularization (changepoint_prior_scale) does the real selection

holidays_prior_scale.note: only meaningful when a holiday frame is supplied

invariances.why: the model is linear in y (Prophet internally rescales y to [0,1] before Stan); forecasts and intervals are equivariant to rescaling the series
a log transform changes additive vs multiplicative structure and the meaning of a linear trend — a modeling choice, not a no-op
curve-fit on timestamps, not lag recursion: missing periods are simply absent rows in (ds, y) — no regular grid is required, the family's distinguishing tolerance
holidays enter via an explicit dataframe and extra regressors must be numeric — no native categorical pathway
Gaussian observation noise around the fitted curve; intervals come from simulating changepoint continuation under the fitted Laplace prior — both are model premises
each requested seasonality needs >=2 full cycles to separate from trend (yearly seasonality wants >=2 years); sub-daily/weekly-only series with yearly enabled overfit the Fourier terms
the last trend segment is extended (with simulated future changepoints widening intervals); logistic growth saturates at the supplied cap instead of extending linearly

featureStats.why: decides which Fourier seasonalities to enable and their prior scale; weak seasonality with seasonality enabled just spends flexibility on noise
sustained slope with visible kinks is Prophet's home turf (piecewise-linear changepoint trend); no-trend series waste its main mechanism
family gate applied per requested seasonality: fewer than 2 cycles of a component makes that Fourier block unidentifiable against trend
the share of missing periods is precisely where Prophet earns its slot over ARIMA/ETS — high gap_fraction routes here rather than to interpolation-hungry recursions

modelMetrics.why: the family's honest scoreboard — Prophet's decomposition prettiness does not exempt it from having to beat repeating last season, evaluated on a time-ordered holdout

edgeCases.condition: requested seasonality with < 2 full cycles of history
edgeCases.behavior: Fourier terms unidentifiable; seasonality absorbs trend
trend chases noise; intervals explode at horizon
edgeCases.note: time-ordered CV over the documented [0.001,0.5] range

edgeCases.behavior: degenerate fit (internal y-scaling divides by max|y|; zero-variance series is meaningless to decompose)
import/fit fails at the Stan backend
edgeCases.note: driver availability gate — see deps flag; component may remain Planned

deps: prophet>=1.1 — HEAVY: pulls cmdstanpy + a compiled CmdStan toolchain (optional extras file; may remain Planned permanently per the plan's risk register)
driver.wrapperNeeds: series adapter: (time_col, value_col) -> ds/y frame; horizon -> make_future_dataframe(freq); component extraction from the predict frame; NO pickle anywhere in the wrapper
driver.threadSafety: fit shells out to a Stan subprocess; one fit per process is safe, parallelize across processes

placementClaims.why: gaps are handled natively (nativeNaN true) — imputing first only fabricates observations the likelihood would otherwise correctly ignore
log transform stabilizes variance and is the alternative to seasonality_mode='multiplicative'; a deliberate structural choice
Prophet rescales y internally before Stan; external standardization changes nothing
single numeric series; holidays/extra regressors enter through dedicated numeric channels, not a preprocessing encode step
